system_description.narrative_title: Escalating U.S.–Canada Trade War and Economic Fallout
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid escalation of U.S. trade measures under the Trump administration and Canadian retaliatory tariffs is driving market moves, corporate responses (job announcements, stock volatility, boycotts) and political signalling ahead of U.S. midterms. The conflict is an open system where policy actions, commercial exposures, financial markets and domestic political incentives interact in reinforcing feedback loops that amplify economic pain and political pressure on both sides.
system_description.scope: Policy-driven trade barriers and countermeasures between the U.S. and Canada, affected goods and sectors, exposed firms and jobs, market/FX reactions, and the political incentives and communications that motivate further policy.
system_description.super_system: International political-economy and global trade regime
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. domestic politics and electoral incentives (midterms, MAGA policy)
Canadian domestic economy and industrial policy
Global corporate supply chains and manufacturing decisions
evidence_headlines: Bombardier’s stock drops as the U.S.-Canada trade war intensifies. Here’s what Trump is targeting next.

US bans Canadian dairy, motorcycles and most alcoholic beverages - ft.com

variables.name: Tariff intensity
variables.description: The average level of ad valorem and specific tariff burdens applied to traded goods targeted by policy measures.

variables.name: Non-tariff restriction intensity
variables.description: The frequency and severity of regulatory bans, quotas, import standards, and other non-tariff measures affecting cross-border commerce.

variables.name: Policy escalation rate
variables.description: The rate at which new trade measures and countermeasures are introduced over time between the parties involved.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The intensity of short-term electoral and interest-group incentives pushing policymakers toward protectionist or retaliatory actions.

variables.name: Media attention intensity
variables.description: The volume and prominence of news coverage and public discourse about the trade conflict and related economic impacts.

variables.name: Sectoral exposure share
variables.description: The proportion of economic activity or revenues in each sector that is exposed to the affected trade relationship or market.

variables.name: Supply chain disruption level
variables.description: The extent and severity of interruptions to intermediate goods flows, supplier switching costs, and logistical delays.

variables.name: Relocation and investment flow rate
variables.description: The rate at which firms shift production, investment, or jobs across jurisdictions in response to trade policy incentives.

variables.name: Currency volatility level
variables.description: The short-term variability of exchange rates affecting relative prices and competitiveness between trading partners.

variables.name: Equity market volatility
variables.description: The degree of price volatility in listed equity markets driven by policy uncertainty and trade-related news.

variables.name: Consumer boycott activity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of organized consumer and business-level boycotts or purchasing shifts targeting goods from the other side.

variables.name: Bilateral trade volume
variables.description: The aggregate flow of goods and services exchanged between the two trade partners over a given period.

variables.name: Firm tariff cost burden
variables.description: The average direct and indirect cost impact of tariffs and compliance measures on firms operating in affected sectors.

variables.name: Trade dispute filing rate
variables.description: The rate at which formal trade complaints, litigation, and arbitration cases are initiated in response to measures.

variables.name: Policy communication hostility
variables.description: The tone and aggressiveness of official political and bureaucratic communications related to trade policy and measures.

variables.name: Multilateral regime resilience
variables.description: The capacity of international trade institutions, norms, and third-party relationships to absorb, mediate, or limit bilateral trade shocks.

catalysts.title: U.S. 2026 midterm elections
catalysts.description: November 2026 congressional elections that will shape U.S. political incentives and trade rhetoric, tied to Trump’s campaign promises.
catalysts.rationale: Trump links policy promises to midterms, raising electoral pressure and trade rhetoric (headlines on $5,000 dividend and midterm promises).

catalysts.title: GSA removal of Canadian goods from procurement lists
catalysts.description: Implementation of directives to strip Canadian suppliers from U.S. federal procurement lists, reducing market access via procurement channels.
catalysts.rationale: Trump directed GSA to remove Canadian goods from agency lists (headline: Trump directs GSA to take steps...).

catalysts.title: High-profile Canadian investor summit
catalysts.description: Planned investor summit aimed to attract investment and offset trade shock, potentially shifting relocation and capital flows.
catalysts.rationale: Canada pins hope on high-profile investor summit to turbocharge economy (headline: Canada Pins Hope for Economic Turbocharge...).

catalysts.title: Continued rounds of trade measures and retaliation
catalysts.description: An ongoing cycle of U.S. bans and Canadian retaliatory tariffs and countermeasures as talks stall, driving further restrictions.
catalysts.rationale: U.S. bans and Canada’s retaliatory tariffs take effect while talks stall (headlines on bans, retaliatory tariffs, talks stall).

catalysts.title: Bombardier U.S. production and hiring decisions
catalysts.description: Bombardier's choices to expand U.S. hiring or shift production in response to political pressure and boycotts will affect cross-border supply links.
catalysts.rationale: Bombardier faces U.S. pressure and calls for boycotts while pledging to fill 500 U.S. jobs (headlines on Bombardier stock, hiring, boycott calls).

catalysts.title: Canadian dollar volatility spike
catalysts.description: Near-term depreciation and heightened exchange-rate swings for the Canadian dollar amid trade disruptions and market reaction.
catalysts.rationale: Canadian dollar edges lower as trade war intensifies and markets react to bans and tariffs (headline: Canadian dollar edges lower).

catalysts.title: Wave of formal trade dispute filings
catalysts.description: Expected increase in formal complaints and arbitration filings at multilateral fora in response to bans and retaliatory tariffs.
catalysts.rationale: U.S. bans and Canada’s tariffs likely prompt formal disputes (headlines on bans, retaliatory tariffs, tribunal rulings).

catalysts.title: Mobilization of consumer and business boycotts
catalysts.description: Organized boycotts and calls to avoid counterpart goods (e.g., Bombardier) intensify consumer and business purchasing shifts.
catalysts.rationale: Trump calls for Bombardier boycott and public rhetoric encourage consumer mobilization (headlines on boycott calls, Bombardier).

catalysts.title: Bank of Canada/Canadian policy backstops
catalysts.description: Monetary or fiscal interventions promised to backstop the economy in response to trade shock, likely to be announced or expanded.
catalysts.rationale: Carney vows to backstop economy as trade row escalates, implying near-term policy support (headline: Carney Vows to Backstop Economy).
